messages:
Lena (oncall): Noticed a p95 and throughput dip for embeddings-service at ~03:22 UTC. Pattern looks different from cache-warmup—lat spikes correlate with a sudden rise in very long requests (token > 2k). Opening a thread to decide SLO handling + owners.

Carlos: I see it in traces. Topology shows the shard handling long sequences got backed up and spilled over to slower hosts. Queue length jumped.

Mei: Can we confirm customer spread? If it's a small number of heavy requests we should throttle at edge rather than change SLOs.

Lena (oncall): Quick breakdown: 72% of long requests came from three API keys tied to one integration. No single one exceeds allowed rate but combined pattern during the promo caused simultaneous long sequences.

Raj: Suggestion: short-term mitigation = enforce max-seq-size at router (clip >1500 tokens) + a 72h temporary SLO exception window. That gives us time to deploy a soft-throttle + fallback model variant for very long inputs.

Mei: +1 to router clipping as an opt-in configurable for Dedicated customers. For Hosted, we should post a status note before changing SLOs.

Carlos: I'll own the router rule change and test in canary. Plan: add request-size histogram metric and a rate limiter rule with burst=3. ETA: 6h.

Lena (oncall): Who can handle SLO change + status communication? We need to decide p95 target and whether to mark this as maintenance override in error budget.

Mei: I can handle the SLO dashboard update and status page blurb. Proposal: relax p95 from 300ms -> 500ms for 72h. Mark the window as "incident override" and exclude from monthly burn. Owner: Mei, ETA: 2h.

Raj: I'll draft a short-term fallback: route >1500 token requests to smaller beam model (cheaper but faster). RFC for fallback strategy -> Owner: Raj, ETA: 10d.

Lena (oncall): Ops-Bot, create ticket with subtasks: router-limit (Carlos), SLO comms (Mei), histogram panel (Carlos), fallback RFC (Raj).

Ops-Bot: Created ticket REDW-3499 with subtasks REDW-3500 (router-limit) -> Carlos, REDW-3501 (SLO update & comms) -> Mei, REDW-3502 (request-size histogram) -> Carlos, REDW-3503 (fallback RFC) -> Raj. Due dates assigned.

Carlos: Posting the alert query I'm using for the histogram and queue watch:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=\"embeddings\"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Ping me if you want access to the canary logs.

Mei: For transparency, I'll add an internal console note that Dedicated customers can opt-out of the temporary SLO change. Also adding a link to the support playbook.

Lena (oncall): On error-budget accounting: I'm okay marking this 72h window as an override if we capture full justification in the postmortem and ticket. Anyone object?

Raj: No objection. Let's be explicit in postmortem so finance/ops reporting doesn't get confused.

Carlos: Router rule pushed to canary cluster. Observing reduced queue lengths. Will roll to prod after 2h of stable metrics.

Mei: SLO dashboard note posted and status page published: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/REDW-3499

Lena (oncall): Scheduling a 72h check-in to evaluate: 1770196399 (72h). Ops-Bot set a reminder.

Raj: RFC skeleton started in doc: https://redwood.docs/rfc/fallback-variants. Will circulate tomorrow.

Ops-Bot: Reminder scheduled: 1770196399 - "72h SLO review for long-sequence incident"

Lena (oncall): Thanks team. Attaching this thread to the incident postmortem and updating the tracking board. Keep tickets updated as you make progress. :thumbsup:
